criterion_notes.c1: Examines household and village-level sanitation (toilet construction and use) and drinking-water service infrastructure (piped water supply, overhead tanks, borewells, and tube wells) alongside roads and solar street lights in rural Koraput, Odisha.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain/broad wording of Criterion 2 (plain=yes) because it examines Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) mandated under Section 135/Schedule VII of India's Companies Act, 2013, corporate CSR portal reporting, and corporate-state partnership arrangements in rural infrastructure provision. However, it fails the active 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type reading of Criterion 2 (narrow=no): the Companies Act 2% corporate profit-spending mandate operates as macro CSR financing background and accounting classification, while the empirical village-level analysis evaluates generic CSR project delivery (one-time physical construction quality, lack of community consultation/participation, failure to assess groundwater levels, and lack of post-installation maintenance), not a rule-type mechanism directly governing water or sanitation service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure rules, tariffs/cost-recovery, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure).
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary qualitative empirical fieldwork (interviews, focus group discussions, and field observations across 264 sampled beneficiary households in 8 villages) combined with secondary quantitative analysis of CSR expenditures from the Odisha State CSR Portal (Go Care) and company annual reports (2014-2020).
criterion_notes.c4: Reports qualitative community-level outcomes on toilet usability vs. continued open defecation (due to missing piped water connections to toilets and poor construction quality) and drinking-water availability, continuity, and functionality (defunct piped water supply systems, non-functional borewells/tube wells, and continued reliance on unsafe stream/river water vs. working stream-based piped supply in one village).
criterion_notes.c5: Population and unit of analysis (264 sampled rural households across 8 villages in Koraput district, Odisha, plus district-level company CSR expenditures), exposure (CSR rural infrastructure projects implemented by HAL and NALCO), outcomes (qualitative water infrastructure functionality and toilet usage), and study design (mixed-methods secondary expenditure analysis and cross-sectional qualitative fieldwork) are identifiable.

evidence_quotes.quote: The seminal contributions of these two industries in four major areas, i.e., construction of toilets, construction and repair of roads, installation of solar lights and construction and repair of water service infrastructure, have been analysed in this article.

The Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) guidelines floated through the Companies Act, 2013 made it mandatory for CSR units to engage in rural development activities notified in Scheduled VII of the Act.

But, the corporates were found constructing the physical structure through CSR, focusing on quantity aspects, and forgot about other associated responsibilities and quality of rural infrastructure, which are considered major shortfalls of these programmes.

evidence_quotes.quote: This empirical data has been collected from the sample beneficiary households through interviews and focus group discussions, coupled with the field experiences and notes prepared during his field visits and observation.

It has been found from the study areas that corporate constructed toilets at the backside of houses without any water supply system nearby. The villagers of Kapsiput cited the difficulty to collect water from open water sources located far away in the absence of piped water supply, and added that most of them, thereby, prefer open defecation.

evidence_quotes.quote: The overhead water tank and piped water supply system at Kapsiput villages have not been functional since its construction. People depend on river and stream water, which is muddy, unhygienic, and unsafe.

raw_response.exposure: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) rural development infrastructure projects implemented by HAL and NALCO under India's Companies Act, 2013 (construction of toilets, roads, solar street lights, and village water supply infrastructure, alongside CSR portal financial reporting)
raw_response.outcome: Qualitative beneficiary-reported functionality, reliability, and use of constructed toilets (continued open defecation vs. toilet adoption due to absence/presence of piped water and construction quality) and drinking-water infrastructure (defunct borewells/tube wells and non-functional or polluted piped systems vs. continuous piped water supply)
raw_response.population_and_sample: Rural beneficiary communities and households in 8 purposively selected villages (4 in HAL Koraput area, 4 in NALCO Damanjodi area) in Koraput district, Odisha, India (264 randomly selected households), plus secondary CSR expenditure records for 7 companies in Koraput (2014-15 to 2019-20)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E03 (Wrong exposure) per the 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type clarification of Criterion 2. Although the study empirically examines rural household sanitation and drinking-water infrastructure outcomes in Odisha in the context of mandatory CSR under the Companies Act, 2013 (and would be included under a broad/plain reading of Criterion 2), the Companies Act CSR spending mandate serves only as macro financing/reporting background, while the empirical evaluation of water and sanitation access examines generic CSR project delivery (one-off physical construction quality, lack of community consultation, neglect of groundwater levels, and absence of maintenance) rather than a rule-type legal, administrative, or regulatory mechanism directly governing service access.
raw_response.study_design: Mixed-methods empirical case study combining descriptive secondary CSR expenditure data analysis (2014-2020) with cross-sectional qualitative fieldwork (interviews, focus group discussions, and field observation)
